Thanks again for the call earlier, Marissa. Quick follow-up items from our side as we start to put an internal SLO doc together: 

- Target: we’re aiming for P95 end-to-end latency <= 300ms for typical requests, but we can be flexible if streaming first-token latency is lower (we care about time-to-first-token for UX).
- Context window: most calls will include ~8k tokens of historical context (legal doc snippets + user prompt). Output is typically ~1k tokens.
- Concurrency/throughput: steady-state ~200 RPS, concurrency ~50-100 active sessions; optimistic spikes up to ~400 RPS during batch jobs.
- Streaming: yes, streaming of output is required for the user experience. We need to confirm how Redwood handles first-token streaming vs total completion time.

I attached the draft SLO spreadsheet (FinCo-slo-draft.xlsx) with a few example payloads. Can you confirm whether these numbers are realistic for your hosted offering or if we should consider Dedicated/Private? Also: any special tokenization considerations for our legal PDFs?

Next steps: if you can send a short benchmarking plan (what you need from us: sample inputs, expected concurrency profile, preferred test window), we’ll prioritize providing those samples.

Thanks,

Hi John — great talking earlier. Short recap and proposed next steps: 

Recap: you’re targeting P95 <= 300ms (time-to-first-token ideally <200ms), ~8k token input, ~1k token output, streaming required, steady 200 RPS with spikes to ~400.

What we can do next:
- Benchmark plan: we can run a short perf-run against our hosted environment and a Dedicated config. For hosted, we’ll test our best-performing open model variant + streaming. For Dedicated, we’ll test an optimized quantized variant that typically reduces token compute.
- What we need from you: 3 representative payloads (we can use the samples in your SLO spreadsheet), a typical concurrency profile (sessions vs parallel requests), and a 2-hour window we can run a sustained load test.
- Timing: we can get initial bench results in 3 business days once we have samples + preferred test window.

Preliminary notes on context/window latency: in our experience, increasing input context from 4k -> 8k tokens usually increases per-token compute and KV-cache sizes; that disproportionately impacts tail latency under high concurrency. Streaming time-to-first-token is mostly bounded by decoder startup + first attention pass; for many models we can get first-token streaming under 200ms on Dedicated hardware for short prompts, but with 8k input and high concurrency the p95 will rise unless we adjust batching and caching.

I’ve attached a quick PDF with our typical latency bands for 4k/8k/16k contexts (redwood-latency-bench-quicklook.pdf). Neha and Ethan, can you own the bench run?

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

Hi John — thanks for the details and for uploading the samples. I’m happy to run the bench. A few tech notes / asks before we schedule: 

1) Tokenization and padding: please confirm whether the 8k token estimate is using your canonical tokenizer (we’ll need raw text samples or tokenized counts). If the legal snippets include many non-ASCII characters we’ll see higher token counts.

2) Streaming behavior: we support chunked token streaming over our API. For time-to-first-token we track two metrics: (a) time-to-first-byte on the streaming connection and (b) time-to-first-token decoded. Under high concurrency the first-byte metric can be improved by reserving burst capacity or reducing batching windows.

3) Concurrency pattern: are 200 RPS spread across many short requests (e.g., 50ms model time) or longer-running completions (several seconds)? That changes how we configure autoscale/worker concurrency.

Proposed bench plan: 
- Day 1 (2 hours): hosted perf run at steady 200 RPS with 8k input, 1k output (redacted payloads). We’ll capture p50/p95/p99 time-to-first-token and total completion times.
- Day 2 (2 hours): spike tests (400 RPS) and a Dedicated config run to compare.

We usually see p95 first-token for 8k input on hosted fall between 300-800ms depending on model variant and concurrency; Dedicated quantized variants often cut that by ~30-50% for decoder startup and per-token compute. If your goal is p95 <=300ms consistently we may recommend Dedicated with a quantized model or a model with a smaller decoder footprint.

If that plan sounds good, send a 2-hour preferred window (we have slots Wed 22 Jul 13:00-16:00 PDT or Thu 23 Jul 09:00-12:00 PDT).

Thanks,
